assessments.reason: Adds server-only text routes for /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml; no rendered page, store, or style output changes
assessments.consumers: server/routes/robots.txt.ts serves GET /robots.txt (text/plain) and server/routes/sitemap.xml.ts serves GET /sitemap.xml (application/xml); both are consumed only by crawlers. A repo-wide search for robots, sitemap and crawlPolicy finds only these two routes, the pure helper server/utils/crawlPolicy.ts, and tests/crawl-policy.spec.ts; no page, component, composable, store, layout, or stylesheet reads or links these URLs, public/ has no robots.txt, and no page route matches these paths. The sitemap route reads the static read-only mockProducts array (alias or _id) and writes nothing; the cache-policy middleware is scoped to /api and does not run for these paths. No HTML, cart, checkout, order, or shared style output changes, so the home, search, product, cart and orders screenshot groups cannot observe a difference. Runtime evidence from a fresh built server: /robots.txt 200 text/plain; charset=utf-8, /sitemap.xml 200 application/xml; charset=utf-8 with 26 URLs (/, /search and 24 product aliases), each URL returning 200, and no dashboard, checkout, cart or auth paths listed.

assessments.reason: Payment labels and checkout recovery UI change; select the representative order-history visual group and verify failure/label surfaces directly outside the screenshot matrix.
assessments.consumers: Payment state contracts and preparation/restart recovery flow into persisted Order truth displayed by customer order history, so select its orders visual group. Public new/restart/resume responses normalize through useOrder and cartStore into /checkout/fail; scoped desktop/mobile browser cases cover cart/quote/recovery/unknown errors, no-ID retry cleanup, unknown-ID navigation, and successful/rejected known cancellation and authentication redirects without duplicate requests; failure context clears before the API client can redirect. getPaymentStatusById feeds transaction options and the repaired /dashboard/customers/customer-001 RecentTransactions panel and /order-summary/ord-1 tracking dialog. Direct browser tests cover actual known/unknown labels and reject numeric-string/array/null/missing statuses with neutral tracking indicators; these consumers are outside the visual matrix and are not proved by the orders screenshot. Catalog/product rendering, cart line totals, shared layouts/styles, dependencies and provider activation are unchanged; home/search/product/cart screenshots do not exercise these contract-only effects. Corrupt stored states retain conservative recovery and refuse provider/fulfillment side effects; PostgreSQL tests prove rollback and refusal. No storefront-wide screenshot matrix is needed.

assessments.reason: New gated owner refresh composes existing checkout finalization/terminalization; select persisted order history and revision-aware cart consumers. No templates or existing client calls change.
assessments.consumers: POST /api/orders/:id/refresh-payment is a new owner-authenticated default-off Stripe route, not yet referenced by pages/composables (UI integration is #556). Its enabled path reuses existing Payments reconciliation and checkout finalization/terminalization: inventory reservation commit/release, paid Order projection, claim state, and best-effort revision-aware Cart cleanup. Existing /control-panel/orders and cart rendering are representative visible read consumers, so select orders and both cart viewports. Real source HTTP/PostgreSQL tests prove provider-return success/crash retry/cancellation/unknown/REFUND and no credentials or confirmation authority; current built runtime must separately prove unauthorized/default-off responses and the normal mock checkout success consumer. readOrderPaymentState keeps its public state shape/classification and has no existing client reference; only the internal snapshot carries validated identity. Catalog pricing, product templates, layouts/styles and storefront client paths are unchanged; no existing UI calls this gated endpoint, and provider activation remains off. No visual baseline update is intended.

assessments.reason: Refresh review repairs affect persisted order recovery and cart cleanup; shared owner extraction preserves resume/restart authentication. Select cart and order-history consumers.
assessments.consumers: The refresh endpoint has no existing client caller and remains default-off. Fresh persisted state determines finalization or cancellation; completed replays recover revision-aware cart cleanup without repeating inventory/order fulfillment. Cart desktop/mobile and order-history visuals exercise the affected persisted-state consumers. The shared trusted-owner helper is used by refresh, resume and restart; PostgreSQL HTTP suites cover their authentication and owner isolation, and current built runtime checks unauthorized/default-off boundaries plus existing mock checkout success. Public state shape and UI templates/styles/catalog rendering remain unchanged. Provider failures and unavailable application consequences become recovery-required; unknown provider state cannot override fresh completed/canceled local truth. No visual baseline changes are needed.

assessments.reason: Full Refund is an internal default-off capability; verify representative existing paid checkout read consumers after additive schema/provider composition changes.
assessments.consumers: The new stripeRefunds.requestFullRefund export has no route, UI, webhook or application caller in this slice. It writes only its Payments-owned checkout_refunds financial fact and calls the existing Checkout-owned compensation recovery transition, requiring a previously established REFUND and held Order. Payment stays PAID; no Order settlement, inventory/cart mutation, public response or template/style change is introduced. Existing refresh compensation classification can read the claim recovery flag, but no existing browser caller reads that new gated capability. The SDK factory extraction preserves PaymentIntent behavior and remains default-off in mock runtime. Focused isolated PostgreSQL tests exercise enabled refund behavior, durable authorization, full immutable amount/identity, concurrent/lost response/expiry races and migration preservation. Current built mock checkout and cart/order screenshots verify representative existing consumers after the additive migration. Catalog/product/home templates, styles and money are unchanged; broader screenshots would not exercise this internal operation. No baseline updates.

assessments.reason: Refund review repairs preserve provider identity through Checkout transitions and distinguish in-flight conflicts; exercise existing cart/order read consumers after additive schema/recovery guard changes.
assessments.consumers: The Refund capability still has no public route, UI or webhook caller. Known Refund identity/status reconciliation now belongs wholly to Payments and cannot be lost when Checkout advances. Creation still requires the Checkout-owned durable REFUND/held-order gate. The existing compensation recovery helper reuses that same gate, with stronger identity/money checks, and can affect the recovery flag read by the internal order payment-state classifier; its public shape and current default-off runtime boundaries are unchanged. Refund preparation/persistence does not settle Orders or mutate cart/inventory/Payment PAID. New migration008 preserves007 history and constrains only checkout_refunds; unknown legacy timestamps become epoch, never renewed replay permission. Focused isolated PostgreSQL tests cover overlap409, state-advance/known-ID recovery, requires_action, generic failure, financial/migration invariants and existing paid-compensation consumers. Fresh built mock checkout and cart desktop/mobile plus order-history mobile visuals cover existing rendered consumers after the schema/helper changes. Catalog/products/styles/layouts are untouched and would not exercise this internal capability; no baseline updates.

assessments.reason: Head-only SEO change: document title, meta, canonical link and X-Robots-Tag response headers; no rendered body markup, styles, data or client requests change.
assessments.consumers: usePageSeo is called from pages/index.vue, pages/search.vue and pages/product/[slug].vue; usePrivateRouteSeo from app.vue. Both only register useSeoMeta/useHead entries (title, description, robots, og:*, twitter:*, canonical, optional ld+json script), all inside <head>. Templates of these pages, the layout and app.vue template are untouched; product data loading (useAsyncData) is unchanged and only read by computed SEO values. nuxt.config routeRules keep the existing /dashboard/** (appMiddleware auth, ssr:false) and /product/categories (appMiddleware auth) rules and only add an X-Robots-Tag header per private prefix (unit-tested merge; built-runtime curl shows the same 302 auth redirects and dashboard SPA shell). runtimeConfig.public.siteUrl is read only by usePageSeo. Screenshots capture body pixels, not head tags or response headers, so the home/search/product/cart/orders groups cannot observe this change; built-runtime curl and Playwright client-navigation checks cover the head output instead. No baseline updates.

assessments.reason: Search gains a compact visible page h1 above the filters, shifting the search layout; the header mega-menu banner heading changes tag only. Select the search visual group (both viewports).
assessments.consumers: components/search/Heading.vue is rendered only by pages/search.vue, between SearchBreadcrumbs and SearchFilters, so only /search routes shift; the search visual group covers that route at desktop and mobile. BannerNew.vue is rendered only by DektopPopoverContainer.vue inside the desktop products mega-menu (closed by default, not opened in any screenshot); its h1 became an h2 with identical classes (Tailwind sets sizes explicitly, preflight resets heading styles) so there is no visual change, and aria-labelledby=hero-title still resolves to the same id. Home, product, cart and orders pages are unchanged; runtime browser checks cover h1 counts on home, search and product at 1280px and 390px, with the mega-menu open.
